title: Market before breakfast
text:
Before the sun has climbed the hill,
the market lanes are cool and grey.
Ibu Rina lights her lamp
to chase the sleepy night away.

The mangoes glow like little suns,
the beans lie in their tidy rows,
and chillies pile in crimson heaps
that tickle every passing nose.

The baker pulls his bread out hot,
the whole street fills with golden smell.
A boy pedals past with a rattling cart
and rings his little bell.

"Fresh eggs!" "Ripe papaya!" "Tea!"
The voices rise and rise and fall,
like birds that argue in a tree,
they chatter, laugh and call.

A fishmonger tips his silver catch
on ice, and the crates are stacked up high.
The cats come creeping round his feet
and watch him with a hopeful eye.

Rina counts her coins with care
and slips them in her pocket deep.
Then Grandma comes with a wicker bag
and haggles till the price is cheap.

A small girl sits on her father's arm
and points to a mango, ripe and round.
"That one!" she says, and the seller laughs
and passes it down without a sound.

By eight o'clock the sun is high,
and shoppers' bags are full and wide.
The baskets, once so heaped and bright,
have empty bottoms deep inside.

Now stalls are folded, lanes are swept,
and Rina yawns and stretches tall.
The market sleeps till dawn comes round,
and quiet falls on one and all.
